expectation: CD69 is a membrane activation marker on a subset of lymphocytes (T, B, NK). It should give a bright ring on scattered single cells, mostly in the gut lamina propria and lymphoid aggregates, and it should not light epithelium or the background.
observed: A: the tissue outline carries a faint yellow haze, plus a large diffuse glow and stripes across the empty slide. B/C: discrete bright ringed cells, scattered in the stroma and lamina propria around crypts, with the epithelium left dim. D: bright membrane rings on individual cells. E: many bright ringed cells that mostly do not overlap the dim CD19 signal.
why: Discrete, bright, membrane-ringed single cells sit in the lamina propria while the epithelium stays dim, as expected for CD69 on lymphocytes.
notes: Sharp membrane rings on scattered stromal lymphocytes, in the lamina propria and sparing the epithelium. The haze and stripes in A are background. CD19 is faint in E, so the co-expression check is uninformative.
